title: Why Strange Beds Wake Half Your Brain
debate_question: On your next trip, would you pack your own pillowcase from home — or let the guard keep watch?

acts.name: 3-Beat Opening: Relatable Hotel Question, Empathy Flip & Early Brain Guard
sentences: Ever sleep terribly your first night in a hotel?
You're not alone.
And no, it's not the bed.
Half of your brain stayed awake on purpose all night — standing quiet guard.

acts.name: Sasaki 35-Sleeper Lab Scan & Right-Side Deep Sleep
sentences: Neuroscientist Yuka Sasaki scanned thirty-five healthy sleepers across their first two nights in a quiet university sleep lab.
On night one, the right side of every sleeper's brain sank into deep, steady sleep.

acts.name: Left-Side Night Sentry, 3x Tripwire Test & Dolphin Cameo
sentences: But the left side? It stayed light and alert, watching the dark room like a night guard.
Play one strange beep into the right ear, and that left side woke sleepers three times faster — like a tripwire!
Dolphins, whales, and migrating birds use that exact trick, resting one half of the brain while the other watches.

acts.name: Left Network Duty & Sound-Center Scanning Mechanism
sentences: You see, inside your head, a daytime network on your left side stays on duty in strange rooms.
Linked straight to your sound center, it keeps scanning every creak in the hallway until morning light arrives.

acts.name: Night-Two Stand-Down & Lab First-Night Data Toss
sentences: By night two in that exact same bed, the guard finally stands down, and both halves sleep deeply.
That's why sleep labs often toss out the first night's data.

acts.name: Pillowcase Trip Question & Answer-Loop Back to S1
sentences: So on your next trip, would you pack your own pillowcase from home — or let the guard keep watch?
Because that restless first night? That's half of your brain staying up to keep you safe.
